ai.description: *Microgecko persicus* reaches 3–4 cm SVL. It is sandy-brown with dark dorsal crossbars and a white underside. Key features include a cylindrical tail and granular scales lacking enlarged tubercles.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Microgecko persicus* is uniquely identified by its distinctively enlarged, plate-like scales on the underside of the tail, which contrast with the granular scales of other species.
ai.habitat: *Microgecko persicus* inhabits arid, rocky landscapes and gravel plains in the Indian subcontinent, typically found in sparsely vegetated scrubland at low altitudes.
ai.behavior: The Persian Dwarf Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to actively hunt small insects across rocky desert terrain.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Microgecko persicus* is oviparous, laying a single-egg clutch. Breeding typically occurs during the warmer months, from spring through early summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Microgecko persicus* is found in the arid regions of southeastern Iran, extending into Pakistan’s Balochistan province and adjacent desert zones at low elevations.
